title: Zuriel SS&S — Worship and Song Study Pathways
description: Original worship-study pathways to accompany songs, hymns and congregational praise. These are not song lyrics or audio recordings.
rightsPolicy: This file contains original study prompts and Bible references only. It does not grant rights to reproduce, distribute, stream or record third-party lyrics or music. Audio remains disabled unless both composition and recording permissions are documented.

pathways.title: Adoration
pathways.focus: Honouring God for who He is, before asking for what we need.
references: Psalm 29:1-2
Psalm 95:1-7
Revelation 4:8-11
pathways.reflectionPrompt: Name three attributes of God shown in the passages. How does each shape worship?
pathways.contextNote: Keep praise rooted in what Scripture reveals about God.

pathways.title: Thanksgiving
pathways.focus: Remembering God's gifts and responding with gratitude.
references: List specific gifts, including mercy, provision, community and endurance.
pathways.reflectionPrompt: Thanksgiving does not require denying grief or hardship.

pathways.title: Confession
pathways.focus: Bringing sin honestly before God and receiving His promised forgiveness.
references: What does confession name? What does it ask God to renew?
pathways.reflectionPrompt: Confession is not self-condemnation; it turns toward God's truth and mercy.

pathways.title: Lament
pathways.focus: Praying honestly through sorrow, fear and unanswered questions.
references: Notice the movement between complaint, remembrance and hope.
pathways.reflectionPrompt: Do not force a quick happy ending onto a lament.

pathways.title: Reverence
pathways.focus: Approaching God with awe, humility and attentive obedience.
references: What does God's holiness reveal, and how does the worshipper respond?
pathways.reflectionPrompt: Reverence is compatible with confident access through Christ.

pathways.title: God's Faithfulness
pathways.focus: Praising God's steadfast character across generations and circumstances.
references: Trace repeated words describing God's steadfast love and faithfulness.
pathways.reflectionPrompt: Do not turn faithfulness into a promise that believers never suffer.

pathways.title: The Lordship of Jesus
pathways.focus: Confessing Jesus as Lord and ordering life around His teaching.
references: What do these texts say about Jesus' identity and authority?
pathways.reflectionPrompt: Worship of Jesus leads to discipleship, not only emotion.

pathways.title: The Cross
pathways.focus: Remembering Christ's self-giving death and the reconciliation it accomplishes.
references: Identify what the texts say Christ bears, gives and reconciles.
pathways.reflectionPrompt: Avoid reducing the cross to a generic symbol of perseverance.

pathways.title: Resurrection Hope
pathways.focus: Celebrating that Jesus is risen and that death does not have the final word.
references: How does resurrection change Christian hope and present conduct?
pathways.reflectionPrompt: Christian hope is grounded in Christ's resurrection, not wishful thinking.

pathways.title: The Holy Spirit
pathways.focus: Worshipping God for the Spirit's presence, guidance and empowering work.
references: What does the Spirit do in each passage?
pathways.reflectionPrompt: Keep the Spirit's work connected to Christ, truth and holy living.

pathways.title: Unity in Worship
pathways.focus: Joining as one body while honouring different gifts and backgrounds.
references: What attitudes protect unity without erasing truth or difference?
pathways.reflectionPrompt: Unity is not uniformity or avoidance of necessary correction.

pathways.title: Worship in Daily Life
pathways.focus: Offering ordinary work, choices and relationships to God.
references: Choose one ordinary activity to offer to God with integrity.
pathways.reflectionPrompt: Worship includes embodied obedience and care for others.

pathways.title: Psalms as Prayer
pathways.focus: Learning the language of praise, trust, confession and lament from Israel's songbook.
references: Which kind of prayer does each psalm teach?
pathways.reflectionPrompt: Read each psalm in its own voice and historical/literary setting.

pathways.title: Singing with Understanding
pathways.focus: Joining heart and understanding in songs shaped by truth.
references: What truths should the congregation understand and remember?
pathways.reflectionPrompt: Music supports worship; it does not replace Scripture or loving action.

pathways.title: Worship and Justice
pathways.focus: Rejecting worship that is separated from righteousness and care for neighbours.
references: What practices does God call His people to change?
pathways.reflectionPrompt: The prophets challenge injustice, not sincere worship itself.

pathways.title: Silence and Listening
pathways.focus: Making space for attentive prayer and obedience before God.
references: What helps the listener become attentive and ready to respond?
pathways.reflectionPrompt: Silence is a practice, not a technique for controlling God's voice.

pathways.title: Pilgrimage and Procession
pathways.focus: Remembering journeys of worship and God's presence among His people.
references: What do journey songs teach about trust, community and hope?
pathways.reflectionPrompt: Ancient pilgrimage practices should not be copied without understanding their covenant setting.

pathways.title: Creation Praise
pathways.focus: Praising the Creator through the witness of the heavens, earth and living creatures.
references: What aspects of creation prompt praise and humility?
pathways.reflectionPrompt: Creation points to the Creator; it is not itself the object of worship.

pathways.title: Hope of God's New Creation
pathways.focus: Looking toward God's promised renewal and dwelling with His people.
references: What is made new, and what suffering is ended?
pathways.reflectionPrompt: Read prophetic imagery carefully; distinguish hope from speculative timetables.

pathways.title: Family and Generational Praise
pathways.focus: Passing on the remembrance of God's works to children and future generations.
references: What story of God's faithfulness can be shared with the next generation?
pathways.reflectionPrompt: Encourage age-appropriate teaching, not pressure or performance.
